account: Nimbus Therapeutics and Schrödinger developed zasocitinib with computational structure-based design. Schrödinger describes free-energy calculations and virtual screening. Takeda's February 2023 closing announcement states an approximately $4 billion upfront payment to acquire the program, with additional contingent milestones. That transaction is not a valuation of the benefit attributable to AI. The Nimbus-funded phase 2b trial, published on 21 August 2024, treated 259 participants. It found a dose response against placebo, including complete clearance in 33% at the 30 mg dose. A Cochrane network meta-analysis by Sbidian and colleagues, published on 6 August 2025, included the phase 2b trial. Its authors declare no ties to the sponsors. They found that tyrosine kinase 2 (TYK2) inhibitors as a class beat placebo for PASI 90, a 90% improvement in the Psoriasis Area and Severity Index score. They rated the certainty of evidence for zasocitinib as low. In an interview with Drug Target Review published on 26 September 2025, a Takeda scientist, Warren Winkelman, described the approach as AI-assisted. These accounts do not isolate the effect of AI from the wider discovery process. Takeda reported on 18 December 2025 that two placebo- and apremilast-controlled phase 3 trials met all 44 ranked secondary endpoints. The sponsor's registration of the LATITUDE Atlas trial lists 606 enrolled participants and gives 22 April 2026 as its primary completion date. It has no posted results. On 14 September 2026 Takeda reported that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration had granted priority review and that the European Medicines Agency had accepted its application. Both were application milestones. On 30 September 2026 Takeda reported that zasocitinib produced complete skin clearance in 36.5% of its LATITUDE Atlas group, versus 13.9% with deucravacitinib, at week 16. The announcement gives analysis groups of 301 and 303 participants. No approval or rejection had been reported by 29 October 2026.

fields.account: Nimbus Therapeutics and Schrödinger developed zasocitinib with computational structure-based design. Schrödinger describes free-energy calculations and virtual screening. Takeda's February 2023 closing announcement states an approximately $4 billion upfront payment to acquire the program, with additional contingent milestones. That transaction is not a valuation of the benefit attributable to AI. The Nimbus-funded phase 2b trial, published on 21 August 2024, treated 259 participants. It found a dose response against placebo, including complete clearance in 33% at the 30 mg dose. A Cochrane network meta-analysis by Sbidian and colleagues, published on 6 August 2025, included the phase 2b trial. Its authors declare no ties to the sponsors. They found that tyrosine kinase 2 (TYK2) inhibitors as a class beat placebo for PASI 90, a 90% improvement in the Psoriasis Area and Severity Index score. They rated the certainty of evidence for zasocitinib as low. In an interview with Drug Target Review published on 26 September 2025, a Takeda scientist, Warren Winkelman, described the approach as AI-assisted. These accounts do not isolate the effect of AI from the wider discovery process. Takeda reported on 18 December 2025 that two placebo- and apremilast-controlled phase 3 trials met all 44 ranked secondary endpoints. The sponsor's registration of the LATITUDE Atlas trial lists 606 enrolled participants and gives 22 April 2026 as its primary completion date. It has no posted results. On 14 September 2026 Takeda reported that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration had granted priority review and that the European Medicines Agency had accepted its application. Both were application milestones. On 30 September 2026 Takeda reported that zasocitinib produced complete skin clearance in 36.5% of its LATITUDE Atlas group, versus 13.9% with deucravacitinib, at week 16. The announcement gives analysis groups of 301 and 303 participants. No approval or rejection had been reported by 29 October 2026.
